taste.name: One loud color, everywhere else quiet
taste.trigger: Deciding how to draw the eye to the single most important action per screen (book, chat, buy).
taste.decision: Chose to reserve lime #C3FB11 for exactly one primary CTA per screen, over using the already-present brand blue more prominently or introducing multiple accent colors for hierarchy.
taste.reason: A patient arriving from a shared link needs one unambiguous next step, not a palette to interpret.
evidence: Lime appears only on the detail page's "Chat now" button (~17.5% of visible area) and nowhere else across 3 pages analyzed
Blue #0056D6 is reused for ~15 other roles (links, secondary buttons, prices) — never promoted to primary-CTA duty

taste.name: Borders do the separating, shadows barely whisper
taste.trigger: Separating 5+ stacked service cards on the store page without the page feeling heavy.
taste.decision: Chose 1px borders + 16px radius as the default card treatment, over drop shadows for depth.
taste.reason: A healthcare-procedure store should read as a calm form, not a shopping app stacked with drop shadows.
evidence: 7 of 8 detected card elements on the store page carry shadow: null
Only the one expanded/primary card ("Dental Smile pack") carries a shadow, and it's rgba(16,24,40,0.06) — barely perceptible

taste.name: Everything lives on an 8px grid, no exceptions
taste.trigger: Three visually distinct surfaces (profile, store, chat), likely built as separate flows.
taste.decision: Constrained every gap/margin/padding to multiples of 4px (dominant values 8/16/24), over letting each surface pick its own spacing rhythm.
taste.reason: Consistent tap targets and breathing room let a patient move between looking at a doctor, buying a service, and chatting without the layout resetting its rules.
evidence: spacingDistribution's top values are 8px, 16px, 24px on all 3 pages, captured independently

taste.name: One typeface, three weights, no exceptions
taste.trigger: Needing to express hierarchy (headline vs. button label vs. body copy) across three different surfaces.
taste.decision: Chose a single custom rounded family (madeCarvingSoft) in only 300/400/600, over pairing a display font with a body font or adding a 700 bold weight.
taste.reason: A single rounded typeface system reads as approachable rather than corporate — a deliberate choice for patients who may already be anxious about a medical decision.
evidence: uniqueFamilies is 100% single-family across all 3 pages (129/59/101 sampled elements)
weightDistribution caps at 600; only one incidental 700 appears
